messages.author: 865451ff948b0e2a
messages.subject: controlling the output with RApacheOutputErrors
parts:
I have activated ROutputErrors in r.conf and it works as is suppose to
do.

When I have an error I get this:

Oops!!! rApache has something to tell you. View source and read the
HTML comments at the end.

And in the source code I get the error.

<!-- Error in library(micEconAids) : there is no package called
'micEconAids' Traceback: 5: stop(txt, domain = NA) 4:
library(micEconAids) 3: eval(expr, envir, enclos) 2: eval(i, envir)
1: sys.source(file = \"/var/www/r/test/25.R\", envir = .rAenv)
-->

I am trying to build a webservice and I would like to have the errors
directly. I am trying to do this in r.conf

RApacheOutputErrors(TRUE,"<p>","</p>")

But I get this error on restart: "Invalid command
'RApacheOutputErrors(TRUE,"<p>","</p>")', perhaps misspelled or
defined by a module not included in the server configuration";

How and where can I use this directive?

Thanks

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: controlling the output with RApacheOutputErrors
parts:
You're supposed to put RApacheOutputErrors function within R handler,
not in apache.conf file, as you probably did. Note that this will
override ROutputErrors directive in apache.conf

> library(micEconAids) 3: eval(expr, envir, enclos) 2: eval(i, envir)
> 1: sys.source(file = \"/var/www/r/test/25.R\", envir = .rAenv)

messages.subject: Re: controlling the output with RApacheOutputErrors
parts:
I'm building a webservice and executing clients scripts which I would prefer not to touch in any way, especially if RApache has including ROutputErrors directive.  You are suggesting to enclose all client code in a tryCatch block and this will bring me to parsing R code, an action that I will prefer not to go into. 

The funny thing is that I have the response, just that I want it with comments tags. Probably I will have to choose between getting an HTTP 200 and parse the comments, or get a 500 and get them from error logs. I still prefer both to entering R code.

Thanks again

Maciej

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: controlling the output with RApacheOutputErrors
parts:
Apache error logs? Usually they are located in /etc/httpd/logs/error_log

I have even set an alias to get last few lines from error log! =)

alias httperror="tail /etc/httpc/logs/error_log"
